summary: CPU design + online research: the FUNDAMENTAL B=1 speed win given we control our own kernels — close native's 2.2x-above-bandwidth-floor gap via megakernel/persistent fusion + B=1 fp8 GEMV efficiency + weight-stream pipelining, lossless

fg.where120msGoes: Native MTP-5 = 218.2 ms/fwd vs the 98.6 ms weight-bandwidth floor (FR13_BEAT_NATIVE_SPEED_DESIGN_BIND.md) = 2.21x the floor, so 119.6 ms/fwd is slack. In absolute terms this slack is exactly native achieving only ~45% of the 273 GB/s peak on its weight stream (26.9 GB / 0.2182 s = 123 GB/s = 45% of peak). That 45% matches the canonical external number: Hazy Research measured vLLM/SGLang at ~50% of H100 bandwidth for single-sequence decode. Decomposition (anchored to the native B=1 nsys profile output/fr13_b1_profile_bind/native + Hazy/MPK literature): (A) NO cross-layer weight PREFETCH, DOMINANT, est ~55-75 ms: 64 layers each launch separate kernels and between them the next weight matrix's DMA does not overlap the current kernel's compute, so every weight tile is cold-fetched (memory pipeline bubbles); this is what a megakernel removes. (B) Skinny-GEMV under-utilization at M=6-10, folded into A not a separable extra-bytes term: weight read is M-independent so M-padding adds no weight bytes, it wastes occupancy/compute and per-launch fixed cost, surfacing as part of the 45%-vs-100% gap. (C) Per-layer kernel-launch + host dispatch, est ~20-40 ms: profile shows 37,807 cudaLaunchKernel over 72 forwards = ~525 host launches/forward, only 868 cudaGraphLaunch (~12/fwd), so native is mostly NOT one FULL captured graph; FR13_OVERHEAD_DECOMP_PLAN.md §2.2 relabeled the old <=2.7% HW-launch claim, measured eager-vs-captured deltas are 56-101 ms (CPU python dispatch + per-layer glue). (D) Per-layer sync/run-ahead/graph-break gaps, est ~15-30 ms: cudaEventSynchronize 26.1 s/477, cudaStreamSynchronize 6.6 s/519, cudaDeviceSynchronize 3.0 s/472, plus graph breaks at vllm::gdn_attention_core / vllm::unified_attention_with_output; much of the 26 s is overlapped output-thread wait (run-ahead preserved), not pure stall. Buckets sum to ~90-145 ms, bracketing the measured 119.6 ms. CAVEAT: the nsys export's per-kernel summary tables are EMPTY (FR13_B1_PROFILE_BIND.md Kernel visibility limit), so GEMM/attention per-kernel times are NOT directly measured; the A/C/D split is EST anchored to runtime-API counts + literature, not a per-kernel trace (the top-30-kernel table is specified but unrun, FR13_OVERHEAD_DECOMP_PLAN Stage 1).
fg.gemvEfficiency: At B=1 native achieves ~45% of the 273 GB/s peak on the full weight stream (26.9 GB / 218.2 ms = 123 GB/s effective). Per-GEMM: fp8 LM GEMMs route through w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm (fp8_utils.py), dispatched via kernels/linear/scaled_mm/triton.py:166-200 (TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel). CRITICAL FINDING: get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs (fp8_utils.py:803) looks up a per-device tuned JSON by device_name and there is NO GB10/sm_121 config present (configs dir has only H100/H200/MI300X/L40S/A100), so GB10 falls to the DEFAULT config (fp8_utils.py:897-904): BLOCK_SIZE_M=64, GROUP_SIZE_M=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=2. At decode M=6-10 with BLOCK_SIZE_M=64 only 9-16% of the materialized M-tile rows are real (offs_am mask, line 764); M-pad wastes COMPUTE + activation re-reads but NOT weight bytes (b_ptrs load is M-independent, lines 768/777). grid = cdiv(M,64)*cdiv(N,128) = a single M-tile: gate_up (N=34816,K=5120,178 MB) = 272 CTAs, down (N=5120,K=17408,89 MB) = 40 CTAs. VERDICT: the GEMV is memory-pipeline-bound (good, it IS reading the weights it must) but under-tiled and launch/occupancy-LIMITED in a RECOVERABLE way: (i) no GB10-tuned config so BLOCK_SIZE_K/num_stages aren't picked for LPDDR5X latency-hiding and num_stages=2 gives shallow double-buffering that only partly hides weight-DMA latency; (ii) each GEMM launches cold with no prefetch from the prior GEMM. Effective single-matrix GB/s is NOT directly measured here (nsys cuda_gpu_kern_sum export EMPTY per FR13_B1_PROFILE_BIND.md). External anchor: DeepGEMM ~2668 GB/s on H100 (~80% of 3.35 TB/s peak) for fp8; Hazy single-kernel decode 78% of peak. So a well-tuned fp8 decode kernel reaches ~78-80% of peak vs native's 45% here, i.e. roughly 0.55x of achievable single-matrix BW is left on the table; the 45%->~78% recovery is the GEMV-efficiency headroom.
fg.launchPipelineGap: 64 layers (48 GDN + 16 full-attn, full_attention_interval=4, /models/qwen3.6-27b-fp8/config.json), each launching ~5-8 separate kernels (in_proj/qkv, GDN-scan or full-attn, o_proj, gate_up, down, 2x RMSNorm). The native B=1 profile shows ~525 host kernel launches/forward and only ~12 graph-replay launches/forward (868 cudaGraphLaunch / 72 drafts), so native is NOT one contiguous captured forward; large eager/piecewise regions remain with graph breaks at vllm::gdn_attention_core and vllm::unified_attention_with_output (FR13_OVERHEAD_DECOMP_PLAN.md §1.1 splitting_ops). At each of these ~525 boundaries the next layer's weight matrix is cold, no producer kernel issues the DMA of layer L+1 weights while layer L computes. A megakernel/persistent kernel (Mirage MPK; Hazy/ThunderKittens) fuses layers into one on-GPU interpreter and software-pipelines weight DMA against compute across layer boundaries, closing the bubble. RECLAIMABLE: the dominant share of the 119.6 ms slack. Hazy moved single-sequence decode ~50%->78% of peak; applying 78% to our floor gives 98.6/0.78 = 126 ms/fwd = 1.28x floor vs native's 2.21x => ~92 ms/fwd reclaimable of the 119.6 ms. MPK anchor: Qwen3-8B/A100 14.5->12.5 ms vs 10 ms floor (1.45x->1.25x) from megakernelization alone (mirage arXiv 2512.22219; zhihaojia medium). CONSTRAINT (FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP_HYPOTHESES.md ranks 14-18): a true Hopper/Blackwell warp-specialized megakernel is partly BLOCKED on GB10/sm_121 (tcgen05, TMEM, TMA tile control, DSMEM/multicast, clusters >1x1x1, WGMMA absent/restricted; CUTLASS #2947, dgx-spark-playbooks #22, vLLM #22279). The achievable GB10 mechanism is CUDA-graph FULL-capture + async weight-prefetch/persistent grid (cp.async multi-stage buffering, deeper num_stages), NOT a datacenter-Blackwell megakernel. OPT-1 (FR13_BEAT_NATIVE_SPEED_DESIGN_BIND.md) is the first concrete step: removes the committer DtoH+sync that blocks the main thread 91.9% of the window vs native 0.8%, restoring run-ahead, a prerequisite for cross-layer pipelining on the tree path.
fg.achievableFloor: Realistic target: ~126-150 ms/fwd (1.28-1.52x floor), NOT the 98.6 ms floor itself. Native sits at 2.21x floor (218 ms, 45% of peak). Proven external ceiling for a well-pipelined single-sequence decode kernel is 78% of peak (Hazy Look Ma No Bubbles) = 1.28x floor = ~126 ms/fwd; MPK independently lands at 1.25x floor on Qwen3-8B/A100. Adjusting DOWN for GB10 reality (sm_121 lacks the warp-specialization/TMA-multicast that lets Hopper/Blackwell hit 78%, FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP_HYPOTHESES.md ranks 14-18), a realistic GB10 target is the 60-70%-of-peak band = ~140-165 ms/fwd, with ~126 ms as the optimistic stretch if a clean async-prefetch persistent grid lands. Either way that is FAR below native's 218 ms: a realistic ~140-150 ms target is ~1.45-1.55x faster on s/fwd alone, and the cat9 accept edge (~3.18 vs native ~3.07 tok/fwd) compounds it into a larger TPS win. DOMINANT REMAINING FLOOR is twofold: (1) the irreducible weight-bandwidth floor (98.6 ms; reading 26.9 GB once at 273 GB/s, M-independent, dense/non-MoE so no sparsity escape, the hard wall); (2) the GB10-specific kernel-pipelining ceiling, without TMA-multicast/warp-specialization/clusters the last ~20-30 points from ~70% to 100% of peak are very hard to reclaim on sm_121, so the practical asymptote is ~1.3-1.5x floor not 1.0x. Secondary floors: GDN-state HBM amplification on OUR tree path (currently 9.0x native, removable to 1.0x via WY one-pass + accept-only commit, FR13_LOSSLESS_FAST_DERIVATION.md, an OPT-side tax not native's floor) and the bf16 lm-head GEMV over 6-10 rows (2.5 GB M-independent weight read, ~9 ms at peak). All gated behind the lossless 22->3 flip fix landing first (build queued after) and must stay bit-exact: structural/scheduling-only (same ops fused, same reduction order, identical fp8 block-scale math), no precision change.

kt.megakernel:
FEASIBLE-IN-PART, and it is the single largest lever on native's ~120 ms/fwd floor-gap. The megakernel idea = fuse the whole tree-verify forward (or large blocks) into ONE persistent kernel that keeps activations on-chip and software-pipelines the next layer's weight DMA against the current layer's compute, deleting per-layer launch + sync + cold-fetch bubbles.

WHAT CAN BE FUSED given our kernels:
- We control three of the per-layer ops: the GDN tree-scan (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py), the FA2-fork tree attention (fr13_patch_fa2_tree_bias.py), and we can wrap/replace the fp8 GEMV path for in_proj/qkv/o_proj/gate_up/down. So a partial megakernel could fuse, per layer: RMSNorm -> fp8 GEMV (gate_up/down or qkv/o_proj) -> the GDN-scan or tree-attn -> residual, eliminating the intra-layer kernel boundaries and the per-layer torch.empty allocations (FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP_HYPOTHESES #2, already flagged as the capture prerequisite). vLLM's splitting_ops (vllm::gdn_attention_core, vllm::unified_attention_with_output) currently graph-BREAK at exactly these points (FR13_OVERHEAD_DECOMP_PLAN 1.1) so even a layer-block fusion removes real breaks.
- The decisive evidence the gap is fusable: MPK/Mirage (arXiv 2512.22219) on Qwen3-8B/A100 takes 14.5 -> 12.5 ms/token vs a 10 ms weight floor = 1.45x -> 1.25x floor, i.e. ~86% of the theoretical max, from megakernelization ALONE (launch elimination + CROSS-LAYER software pipelining + compute/comm overlap). Hazy's "We bought the whole GPU"/"Look Ma No Bubbles" megakernel (hazyresearch 2025-09-28) takes single-sequence Llama decode from ~50% to 78% of H100 bandwidth, >1.5x, by removing the per-op HBM round-trips and the memory-pipeline bubbles between launches. kog.ai's monokernel hits the same idea (one persistent GPU program, not a sequence of per-op kernels). This is precisely native's disease here: native B=1 reaches only ~45% of 273 GB/s (26.9 GB / 0.2182 s = 123 GB/s) and the nsys profile shows ~525 host launches/forward with only ~12 graph-replay launches/forward (868 cudaGraphLaunch / 72 drafts) = NOT one captured forward.

WHAT BLOCKS A FULL megakernel:
- (1) The 26.9 GB weights MUST still stream once/forward (M-independent, dense non-MoE) -> the 98.6 ms floor is the hard wall; a megakernel can only take us from native's 2.21x-floor toward ~1.25-1.5x-floor, NOT to 1.0x. It removes the BUBBLES, not the bytes.
- (2) On-chip residency: GB10 SMEM/registers cannot hold 26.9 GB of weights, so the win is the PIPELINE (overlap next-layer weight DMA with current compute), not keeping weights resident; only activations + the small GDN recurrent state + the 9-node tree stay on-chip. This is the harder-to-build form.
- (3) The GDN recurrence is a sequential state dependency (S_t depends on S_{t-1}) -> the 48 GDN layers cannot be parallel-fused across the scan dimension; they pipeline layer-to-layer but the within-layer scan stays serial. Our no-copy WY one-pass (FR13_LOSSLESS_FAST_DERIVATION) is what makes the GDN layer a single capturable static-loop kernel that a megakernel can chain.
- (4) The data-dependent ACCEPT branch (path-LCP/commit) is host-Python today (OPT-1 / FR13_GPU_COMMITTER moves it to a Triton kernel + CUDA graph conditional-node so it stops breaking the persistent region).

VERDICT: build the GB10-feasible form = CUDA-graph FULL-capture of the whole tree-verify forward + cross-layer async weight prefetch (cp.async multi-stage / deeper num_stages) + persistent/fused layer blocks, NOT a datacenter-Blackwell warp-specialized megakernel. FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP_HYPOTHESES ranked the full "persistent/megakernel" at #16 (drop) on the grounds that full CUDA-graph capture (#6) reclaims most of the launch win at far lower risk -- that ranking is correct for the LAUNCH share but UNDERWEIGHTS the cross-layer prefetch share (the dominant ~55-75 ms bucket A), which capture alone does NOT close. The honest read: full-capture is the must-do floor; the prefetch-pipeline is the high-value, harder, GB10-constrained stretch. Cite: Mirage MPK arXiv:2512.22219; Hazy hazyresearch.stanford.edu/blog/2025-09-28-tp-llama-main; Ada-MK arXiv:2605.11581; kog.ai monokernel blog.
kt.b1GemvKernel:
FEASIBLE in pure Triton; HONEST expected win = MODERATE, NOT large, and most of it overlaps with what full CUDA-graph capture + a GB10-tuned config already reclaim. The opportunity is real because our tree forward's fp8 GEMMs route through native vLLM's w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm (fp8_utils.py:718-933) -- our patches own only the GDN scan + tree attn, so the LM GEMV path is currently UNOPTIMIZED-for-GB10 native code, not ours.

THE RECOVERABLE INEFFICIENCY (measured, CPU-firm):
1. NO GB10/sm_121 tuned config exists (configs dir has only H100/H200/MI300X/L40S/A100), so the GEMM falls to the DEFAULT (fp8_utils.py:897-904): BLOCK_SIZE_M=64, num_warps=4, num_stages=2. At decode M=6-10 with BLOCK_SIZE_M=64, only 9-16% of the materialized M-tile rows are real (offs_am mask :764) -> wasted compute + activation re-reads (NOT weight bytes; b_ptrs load is M-independent :768/777). num_stages=2 = shallow double-buffering that only partly hides LPDDR5X weight-DMA latency.
2. Each GEMM launches COLD with no prefetch from the prior GEMM (this is the cross-layer pipelining gap, shared with the megakernel front).

WHAT A CUSTOM B=1 fp8 GEMV BUYS, vectorized for the skinny M=6-10 tree-row shape:
- Drop BLOCK_SIZE_M from 64 to the tree-row count (6-10) or M=1-per-program GEMV form -> kills the 84-91% phantom-row waste, frees occupancy for more K-tiles in flight.
- Deeper software-pipelined K loop (num_stages 3-4) to better hide weight-DMA latency on LPDDR5X (273 GB/s but higher latency than HBM).
- Vectorized weight loads + fewer scale/zero reloads -- GemLite's GEMV RevSplit-K idea (load scales once per 2 blocks): pytorch.org/blog/accelerating-llm-inference reports RevSplit-K = +5-8% e2e over the default GEMV and +30-40% over Split-K at B=1, pure Triton, no TMA needed (TMA is "disabled by default, MXFP/NVFP only" in GemLite).
- Avoid the M-config-bucket dispatch overhead.

FRACTION-OF-PEAK ANCHORS: external well-tuned B=1 fp8 decode kernels reach ~78-84% of peak single-matrix BW (Hazy 78%; kog.ai cite a custom GEMV "reading the weight once per batch" going 24% -> 84% bandwidth; DeepGEMM ~2668 GB/s = ~80% of H100 peak for fp8). Native here sits at ~45% on the full weight stream. So the GEMV-efficiency headroom is roughly the 45% -> ~70-80% band on the GEMM slice.

HONEST SPEEDUP ESTIMATE vs the current Triton block GEMM at B=1: this CANNOT be a clean fraction-of-current-GEMM number because (a) the per-kernel GEMM time is NOT directly measured here -- the nsys cuda_gpu_kern_sum export is EMPTY (FR13_B1_PROFILE_BIND Kernel visibility limit), so the GEMV's actual achieved GB/s on GB10 is unmeasured; (b) the weight-byte read is identical (M-independent) so a custom GEMV does NOT reduce the binding HBM metric -- it only recovers occupancy/launch/latency-hiding, which on a bandwidth-bound forward is partly hidden behind the weight stream. REALISTIC: a GB10-tuned config (BLOCK_SIZE_M=tree-rows, num_stages=3-4) is the cheap 80% of the win and is just a config/JSON drop (low effort, lossless -- same fp8 block math); a hand-rolled RevSplit-K-style GEMV adds maybe single-digit-% more e2e on top (GemLite's own +5-8% over default GEMV). The ~2x-of-peak gap (45% -> ~80%) is mostly the cross-layer-prefetch + launch buckets (A+C), NOT the GEMM's internal tiling -- so the custom GEMV's STANDALONE win is the smaller part; it must land together with full capture + prefetch to realize the fraction-of-peak numbers above. Lossless is clean: same fp8 [128,128] block-scale math, pin the K-reduction order to match native's accumulation. FIRST STEP (cheapest, highest-confidence): author a GB10/sm_121 entry in the w8a8_block_fp8 configs dir tuned for M=6-10 -- this alone fixes the default-bucket mis-pick with zero kernel rewrite.
kt.weightPipelining:
PARTIALLY FEASIBLE on GB10/sm_121 but RISK-FLAGGED -- this is the highest-value-per-byte lever (it attacks bucket A, the dominant ~55-75 ms of native's 120 ms slack) yet the exact async primitive it needs is the one that is fragile on sm_121.

THE TECHNIQUE: while layer L computes (on the 273 GB/s stream reading L's weights), issue the DMA for layer L+1's weight matrix into a second buffer, so L+1 starts on warm weights. This is what MPK calls cross-layer software pipelining (arXiv:2512.22219: "begin loading data for the next layer while computing the current one") and Hazy calls removing the memory-pipeline bubbles between launches. It reclaims the share of the 45%-vs-100%-of-peak gap that is cold-fetch stalls between kernel/layer boundaries -- NOT a byte reduction (same 26.9 GB), a latency-hiding reduction.

DOES GB10/sm_121 SUPPORT THE NEEDED PRIMITIVES?
- TMA (cp.async.bulk / tensor-tile descriptors): NO -- absent/unsupported on sm_121 (NVIDIA dgx-spark-playbooks #22: GB10 lacks tcgen05, DSMEM, TMEM, TMA/multicast; ptxas refuses sm_121a for .shared::cluster). So the Hopper/Blackwell TMA-descriptor prefetch path that MPK/Hazy use on H100/B200 is OUT.
- Plain cp.async (Ampere-class async global->shared, the LDGSTS path, what MPK falls back to on A100 -- "integrated asynchronous copies", "manual buffering and synchronization", paged-shared-memory abstraction, NO TMA): the HARDWARE has it, but it is FRAGILE on sm_121 in the Triton toolchain -- vLLM #37431 reports the Mamba-2 Triton kernels (our exact kernel family: _causal_conv1d_fwd, _chunk_scan_fwd, _chunk_state_fwd) crash with cudaErrorIllegalInstruction in ASYNC mode on SM121, fixed only by CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 + --enforce-eager (which costs ~37%: 14 -> 8.8 tok/s). Root cause suspected = missing memory barrier / wrong PTX target in the JIT output for async on sm_121. This is a DIRECT, in-family warning that aggressive cp.async multi-stage pipelining in Triton on GB10 is a live correctness/stability hazard right now.
- Triton num_stages (the portable lever): increasing num_stages from native's 2 to 3-4 is the Triton-level way to deepen the producer-side cp.async double-buffering inside a single GEMV and IS expressible in pure Triton without TMA. This is the SAFE, feasible slice of weight-pipelining: it pipelines the K-loop weight tiles WITHIN a GEMM, partially hiding LPDDR5X latency. It does NOT cross the layer boundary (the big bucket-A win), but it is the realistic GB10 mechanism and is lossless (math unchanged, only staging depth).

FRACTION OF THE LAUNCH/SYNC SLACK RECLAIMED: cross-layer prefetch targets the prefetch bucket (A, ~55-75 ms), which is LARGER than the pure launch+sync buckets (C ~20-40 ms + D ~15-30 ms). A datacenter megakernel reclaims most of A; on GB10, without TMA and with the #37431 async hazard, the SAFELY-reclaimable share is smaller -- realistically the within-GEMM num_stages deepening + full-capture (which removes the launch/sync bubbles C+D outright) get us toward the ~60-70%-of-peak band (140-165 ms/fwd) rather than Hopper's 78% (126 ms). The full cross-layer cp.async prefetch is the stretch that, IF the sm_121 async PTX hazard is resolved (or done in CUDA C++ rather than Triton), could push toward the 126 ms optimistic floor. CAVEAT: actual reclaimed ms is unmeasured here (nsys per-kernel export EMPTY); these are literature-anchored estimates. PREREQUISITE: OPT-1 (FR13_GPU_COMMITTER) must first remove the committer DtoH+sync that blocks the main thread 91.9% of the window (vs native 0.8%), which today defeats run-ahead and would defeat any prefetch pipeline on the tree path.
kt.feasibilityOnGB10:
HONEST per-technique feasibility on GB10/sm_121 (Grace-Blackwell consumer; no Hopper TMA/wgmma, no tcgen05/TMEM/DSMEM/cluster-multicast per dgx-spark-playbooks #22; Triton-based; cutlass-block-fp8 unavailable):

1. FULL CUDA-graph capture of the tree-verify forward -- FEASIBLE NOW, pure Triton, lowest risk, do-first. Removes the per-layer launch (C, ~20-40 ms) + sync (D, ~15-30 ms) buckets = the launch/sync share of native's slack. Blockers are OUR code, not the arch: per-forward torch.empty (fix = preallocate, FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP #2) + the host-Python accept branch (fix = OPT-1 FR13_GPU_COMMITTER + CUDA-12.4 graph conditional-node). vLLM PR #20059 already makes max_query_len>1 decode graph-capturable; our TREE_ATTN is captured via the UNIFORM_BATCH declaration. This is feasible and is the must-do floor.

2. Custom B=1 fp8 GEMV (skinny M=6-10) -- FEASIBLE, pure Triton, no Hopper primitives needed (GemLite RevSplit-K is pure Triton, TMA off by default). The cheapest 80% is a GB10/sm_121 tuned config JSON (BLOCK_SIZE_M=tree-rows, num_stages=3-4) since none exists today (native falls to the BLOCK_SIZE_M=64 default bucket). A hand-rolled RevSplit-K-style GEMV is a moderate add. Lossless = same fp8 [128,128] block math, pinned K-reduction order. Feasible.

3. Within-GEMM weight pipelining via Triton num_stages -- FEASIBLE (pure Triton, expressible without TMA), but bounded to intra-GEMM K-loop latency hiding, not cross-layer.

4. Cross-LAYER async weight prefetch (the big bucket-A win) -- FEASIBLE-WITH-RISK. Needs plain cp.async (Ampere LDGSTS class, which GB10 HW has and MPK uses on A100 without TMA), NOT TMA (which sm_121 lacks). BUT vLLM #37431 shows our exact Mamba/Triton kernel family illegal-instruction-crashes in async mode on sm_121 (workaround = enforce-eager, -37%), so aggressive Triton cp.async multi-stage on GB10 is a live stability hazard. Realistically this slice may need CUDA C++ (not Triton) to be safe, or must wait on the sm_121 async PTX fix.

5. Full warp-specialized megakernel (Hazy/Tawa style, Loader/Consumer/Storer roles) -- INFEASIBLE as built for datacenter Blackwell: Triton warp-specialization (Tawa arXiv:2510.14719, PyTorch warp-spec roadmap) depends on Hopper/Blackwell async references + TMA + mbarrier that sm_121 lacks; FA3/FA4 need WGMMA/tcgen05 absent on sm_12x (CUTLASS #2947, vLLM #22279). The persistent-grid + manual-double-buffer megakernel FORM (MPK on A100, CUDA, no TMA) is architecturally possible on GB10 but is a large CUDA-C++ rewrite with bit-exact reduction-order risk and the #37431 async hazard.

BOTTOM LINE: the GB10-realistic stack = full CUDA-graph capture (now) + GB10-tuned skinny GEMV config (now) + within-GEMM num_stages deepening (now) + (stretch, risk-flagged) cross-layer cp.async prefetch. The datacenter warp-specialized TMA megakernel is OUT. Achievable target = ~60-70% of peak = ~140-165 ms/fwd (1.45-1.65x faster than native's 218 ms on s/fwd), with ~126 ms (1.28x floor) as the optimistic stretch if a clean async prefetch lands -- NOT the 98.6 ms floor itself. The cat9 accept edge (~3.18 vs ~3.07 tok/fwd) compounds any s/fwd win into a larger TPS win. All gated behind the lossless 22->3 flip fix; all must stay bit-exact (structural/scheduling only, identical fp8 block-scale math, pinned reduction order).
kt.priorArt:
Fraction-of-floor / fraction-of-peak achieved by the relevant prior art:

MEGAKERNEL / persistent-kernel LLM decode:
- Mirage Persistent Kernel (MPK), arXiv:2512.22219 (zhihaojia.medium.com; catalyst.cs.cmu.edu/projects/mpk): Qwen3-8B on A100, 14.5 -> 12.5 ms/token vs a 10 ms weight-bandwidth floor = 1.45x-floor -> 1.25x-floor = 86% of theoretical max, from megakernelization ALONE. End-to-end latency up to 1.7x lower than kernel-per-op serving. CUDA-generated. Runs on A100/H100/B200 (Ampere included). Cross-layer pipelining uses manual shared-memory buffering + integrated async copies, NOT TMA -- TMA is only used to ACCELERATE on Hopper/Blackwell and is replaced by async copies elsewhere. This is the cleanest "fraction-of-floor" anchor and proves the mechanism is not Hopper-exclusive.
- Hazy Research "We bought the whole GPU" / "Look Ma No Bubbles" megakernel (hazyresearch.stanford.edu/blog/2025-09-28-tp-llama-main; HN 44111673): single-sequence Llama-1B decode, ~50% -> 78% of H100 memory bandwidth, >1.5x over vLLM/SGLang. Five SM roles (Loader/Consumer/Storer/Controller/Launcher), warp specialization, TMA, async I/O, instruction interpreter. The 78%-of-peak is the proven ceiling for a well-pipelined single-seq decode kernel -- but it REQUIRES Hopper warp-spec + TMA, which GB10 lacks, so it is the H100 ceiling, not a GB10-achievable one.
- Ada-MK, arXiv:2605.11581: adaptive megakernel DAG search, confirms the megakernel-on-newer-arch direction.
- kog.ai monokernel blog (real-time-llm-inference-on-standard-gpus): "token generation runs as one persistent GPU program instead of a sequence of per-op kernels"; a custom GEMV "reading the weight matrix once per batch" goes 24% -> 84% bandwidth utilization; 2,100-3,000 tok/s/request at B=1. CUDA + PTX inline asm (NOT Triton). Reports ~36% MBU on a 2B model in tech preview. Confirms the persistent-program idea and the GEMV "read-once" bandwidth recovery, but their implementation is hand-PTX, not Triton.

B=1 fp8 GEMV fraction-of-peak:
- GemLite (dropbox/gemlite, formerly mobiusml), pytorch.org/blog/accelerating-llm-inference: GEMV RevSplit-K is the best B=1 decode algorithm for packed fp8/low-bit -- +5-8% e2e over the default GEMV kernel, +30-40% over Split-K. PURE TRITON, TMA off by default (MXFP/NVFP only). Tested A100/H100/RTX-PRO-6000/4090. No single fraction-of-peak %, but the read-scales-once-per-2-blocks idea is the portable B=1 lever.
- DeepGEMM (deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM): fp8 ~2668 GB/s on H100 = ~80% of the 3.35 TB/s peak -- the fraction-of-peak a well-tuned fp8 kernel reaches vs native's ~45% here. CUDA/CUTLASS (Hopper).
- General B=1 framing: arithmetic intensity ~1-2 FLOP/byte at B=1 (fp8 ~2), so MBU (memory-bandwidth utilization) is the B=1 metric, not MFU (towardsai LLM Latency Part 1; arXiv:2507.15465). Custom Triton GEMV reading the weight once per batch: 24% -> 84% MBU (kog.ai anchor).

FlashInfer/FlashDecoding B=1 kernels: FlashInfer (arXiv:2501.01005) -- its Blackwell MLA kernels use async copy for page loading, MHA kernels use TMA; the TMA path is Hopper/Blackwell-datacenter and not the GB10 mechanism. The async-copy (cp.async) page-load path is the portable analog.

SUMMARY of fraction-of-floor: native here = 2.21x-floor (45% of peak). Proven ceilings: MPK 1.25x-floor (86%, A100, CUDA, no-TMA-required); Hazy 1.28x-floor (78%, H100, TMA+warp-spec required). GB10-realistic target (no TMA/warp-spec, Triton, #37431 async hazard) = ~60-70% of peak = ~1.43-1.65x-floor = ~140-165 ms/fwd, with ~126 ms (1.28x) as the optimistic stretch -- far below native's 218 ms either way.

optimizations.name: OPT-A: GB10/sm_121-tuned skinny-GEMV config (BLOCK_SIZE_M=tree-rows, num_stages=3-4) for the fp8 w8a8 block GEMM path
optimizations.what: Author a per-device JSON entry (and/or a default-bucket override) for the native vLLM w8a8 block-fp8 kernel that the LM in_proj/qkv/o_proj/gate_up/down GEMMs route through. CONFIRMED on live source: get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs (fp8_utils.py:803) looks up configs/N=...,device_name=<GB10>... and the configs dir contains ONLY H100/H200/H20/B200/L20/L40S/MI300X/MI325X -> NO GB10/sm_121 entry, so GB10 falls to the DEFAULT bucket (fp8_utils.py:897-904: BLOCK_SIZE_M=64, GROUP_SIZE_M=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=2). At decode M=6-10 with BLOCK_SIZE_M=64 only 9-16% of the materialized M-tile rows are real (phantom-row waste); num_stages=2 is shallow double-buffering that only partly hides LPDDR5X weight-DMA latency. Drop BLOCK_SIZE_M to the tree-row count and deepen num_stages to 3-4 to better hide weight-DMA on the K-loop. This is the cheapest ~80% of the GEMV-efficiency win as a config/JSON drop with ZERO kernel rewrite, and it touches NATIVE's own slack (the GEMM path our patches don't own), so it beats native rather than only refunding our tax.
optimizations.msSaved: Modest standalone but it is the cheapest unit of the GEMV-efficiency band: it recovers part of the 45%->~70-80%-of-peak headroom on the GEMM slice. Honest bound: weight bytes are M-independent so this does NOT cut the binding HBM metric; it recovers occupancy/launch-bucket/latency-hiding, much of which is hidden behind the weight stream until full-capture (OPT-C) and prefetch (OPT-D) land. Pin the K-reduction order to native's accumulation so the GEMM output is byte-identical (config change must not reorder the fp32 accumulate). Gate = byte A/B on a single GEMM (same in, compare out bytes) + the per-token argmax-vs-clean-teacher probe on the full forward.

optimizations.name: OPT-B: WY one-pass + accept-only-commit no-copy GDN tree-scan (replace ancestor-replay)
optimizations.what: Replace the current replay _tree_gdn_kernel with the fused no-copy WY/UT one-pass tree kernel (native-basis op-order), publishing the d_v x d_k recurrent state ONLY for the accepted path (1/req, exactly like native). This is OUR kernel and it CUTS the binding HBM metric: the current replay carries per-node fp32 state x9 = GDN-state r+w 9.0x native (+2.416 GB/req = +8.95% of the 27 GB weight stream at B=1, up to +9.664 GB / +35.79% at B=4); WY accept-only commit takes that to 1.0x native (+0.0 GB). NOTE: this is FR13's already-ranked #1 lever; it is a TREE-PATH tax removal (refunds OUR amplification back to native's floor) rather than an attack on native's own 120 ms slack, but it is the prerequisite that lets the GDN layer participate in capture+prefetch and removes the largest OUR-side HBM term.

This attacks bucket A (the DOMINANT ~55-75 ms of native's 120 ms slack: no producer kernel prefetches the next layer's weights today, so every weight tile is cold-fetched). Build the GB10-feasible persistent/fused layer-block form (RMSNorm -> fp8 GEMV -> GDN-scan/tree-attn -> residual chained on-chip with double-buffered weight DMA), NOT a datacenter warp-specialized megakernel.
optimizations.msSaved: Highest-value-per-byte lever: targets bucket A (~55-75 ms). plan.floorApproachBudget: ARITHMETIC. Weight-bandwidth FLOOR = 26.9 GB / 273 GB/s = ~98.6 ms/fwd (M-independent, dense non-MoE; hard wall, the bytes cannot be cut without quantization which is lossy/banned). NATIVE MTP-5 = 218.2 ms/fwd = 2.21x floor = only ~45% of 273 GB/s peak on the weight stream (26.9 GB / 0.2182 s = 123 GB/s). So 119.6 ms/fwd is SLACK above the floor. Bucket decomposition (literature-anchored on the native B=1 nsys runtime-API counts; per-kernel times NOT directly measured -- nsys cuda_gpu_kern_sum export EMPTY): A) no cross-layer weight prefetch ~55-75 ms (DOMINANT, OPT-D target); C) per-layer launch+host dispatch ~20-40 ms (~525 host launches/fwd vs ~12 graph launches/fwd, OPT-C target); D) per-layer sync/run-ahead gaps ~15-30 ms (OPT-C target); B) skinny-GEMV M=6-10 under-utilization folded into A (no weight bytes, OPT-A target). Buckets ~90-145 ms bracket the measured 119.6 ms. PROJECTED s/fwd after the fundamental pass: external ceilings are MPK 1.25x floor (86% peak, A100, no-TMA-required) and Hazy 1.28x floor (78% peak, H100, TMA+warp-spec REQUIRED -> not GB10-achievable). Adjusting DOWN for GB10 reality (sm_121 lacks TMA-multicast/warp-specialization/clusters/WGMMA, ranks 14-18), the realistic GB10 target = 60-70%-of-peak band = ~140-165 ms/fwd (1.42-1.67x floor), with ~126 ms/fwd (1.28x floor) as the optimistic stretch if a clean cp.async cross-layer prefetch lands. So native 218 ms -> realistic ~140-150 ms = ~1.45-1.55x faster on s/fwd ALONE, far below native -- and the cat9 accept edge (~3.18 vs native ~3.07 tok/fwd) compounds it into a LARGER TPS win. The 98.6 ms floor itself is NOT reachable on GB10 (the last ~20-30 points to 100% of peak need TMA-multicast/warp-spec GB10 lacks). VS OPT-1: OPT-1 is the STRUCTURAL-OVERHEAD pass -- it only reclaims our +6.6 ms cat9 tax (224.7 -> ~217-220 ms) back to native PARITY (~218); it does NOT attack native's own 119.6 ms slack. THIS fundamental pass attacks native's 119.6 ms directly, taking 218 -> ~140-165 ms, a fundamentally bigger win than OPT-1's tax-refund.
plan.losslessGate: Gate each fundamental change BIT-EXACT, same discipline as FIX-2/FIX-3 and OPT-1: every change ships flag-gated default-OFF so the default-ON path is provably byte-identical. (1) BYTE A/B ON THE KERNEL (class-10): run the single kernel/op the change touches with identical inputs OFF vs ON and compare OUTPUT BYTES -- for OPT-A a single fp8 GEMM (same M=6-10 activations -> identical fp8 output bytes); for OPT-B the GDN tree-scan per-depth argmax+state vs the native-on-path oracle (splice OFF; fp32 4.19e-9 / 0-flip bar); for OPT-C the captured-vs-eager forward replays identical kernels; for OPT-D the fused layer-block same-in -> same-bytes-out. (2) PER-TOKEN ARGMAX PROBE on the FULL forward (fr13_gold_margin_probe.py + FR13_COMMIT_ARGMAX_GATE, reference = native sequential verify, NOT streamed logprobs): teacher-forced per-token argmax-vs-clean across all 64 layers + final logits, because scalar metrics (accept/event, bag-TV, superset count) are BLIND to small-rate per-token flips. (3) SAME-SEED BYTE-IDENTICAL STREAMS in-process (greedy + t0.6) with accept/event unchanged and regular-decode pristine -- the in-process same-boot gate, never a cross-boot byte-identity gate (fresh B=1 forks are autotune floor, not a behavior change). Pin the fp8 K-reduction order and the GDN within-path solve op-order to native's accumulation; any change that reorders a float reduction is NOT lossless even if math-equal (1-bf16-ULP/layer compounds over ~48 GDN layers to argmax flips). For OPT-A/OPT-D specifically: NO precision/quantization change (that is the banned weight-re-streaming / lossy-fp4 route); structural/scheduling/staging only.
plan.effortRanking: ROI = ms-toward-floor per unit effort. (1) OPT-A GB10-tuned GEMV CONFIG JSON drop -- HIGHEST ROI: a config/JSON drop (smallest effort) that touches NATIVE's own un-tuned GEMM path (CONFIRMED: no GB10/sm_121 config exists, default BLOCK_SIZE_M=64/num_stages=2 mis-picked for M=6-10), lossless by construction, GPU-feasible now, and it is the cheapest ~80% of the GEMV-efficiency band. This is the right B=1 GEMV-class build to do BEFORE any megakernel. verify.losslessRealism: Mixed by opt. OPT-A (GEMV config JSON drop): lossless ONLY IF the new config does not change the K-reduction. Verified at fp8_utils.py: the accumulator is fp32 (line 774) and tl.dot accumulates in fp32 with per-block scale applied per K-iter (line 784); BLOCK_SIZE_K=group_k=128 is pinned by the block-scale contract (BLOCK_SIZE_K must divide block_size[1]), so changing BLOCK_SIZE_M / GROUP_SIZE_M / num_warps / num_stages does NOT reorder the K-accumulation — those are tiling/scheduling-only. THIS IS LOSSLESS BY CONSTRUCTION. BUT the catch the design under-weights: deepening num_stages (OPT-D1) changes the software-pipeline depth of the SAME K-loop; that is still the same reduction ORDER (sequential over k), so it is also bit-safe — confirmed. RED FLAG retained: any RevSplit-K / Split-K GEMV variant (mentioned as the OPT-A stretch and in GemLite) DOES split the K-reduction across CTAs and add a cross-CTA combine = DIFFERENT fp32 accumulation order = NOT bit-exact to the current single-CTA-over-K kernel. The design must hard-exclude Split-K/RevSplit-K from the lossless path; only the JSON-meta tuning of the existing single-K-CTA kernel is lossless. OPT-B (WY GEMV/GDN rewrite) is the genuinely hard one for bit-exactness — it reorders the within-path solve entirely; CPU-proven at fp32 4.19e-9 / 0-flip on the NATIVE basis only (the rescaled basis blows exp(|G|)=46573x at depth 64, UNSAFE), and the bf16 boundary is 6.10e-5 with 2/9 flips, INSIDE native's 9.55e-5 self-noise — i.e. argmax-lossless-within-floor, NOT abs-0.0. That matches the FR13 within-floor bar but is weaker than 'byte-identical'; it must gate per-depth argmax vs the native-on-path oracle, not max_abs. OPT-C/OPT-D2 (capture / cross-layer prefetch): structural, replay identical kernels, lossless by construction PROVIDED the fused layer-block does not re-tile a reduction; a fused persistent layer-block (D2) carries real bit-exact reduction-order risk and is flagged hard.
verify.feasibilityHonest: The MEGAKERNEL is NOT feasible on GB10 and the repo's OWN binding doc already says so — the design partially contradicts it. FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP_HYPOTHESES.md (which the design cites) explicitly DROPS: persistent-kernel/megakernel (rank 16, 'no HBM cut; capture gets most of the launch win with less risk + no sm_121 landmine'), TMA/cp.async.bulk cross-layer staging (rank 14, 'moves the SAME bytes = zero HBM reduction'), Blackwell TMA state (rank 15, 'ptxas refuses for sm_121a'), multicast/DSMEM/clusters (rank 18, GB10 limited to 1x1x1), and warp-specialized FA3/FA4/tcgen05 (rank 17, 'structurally unbuildable on GB10'). So a true datacenter-Blackwell warp-specialized TMA megakernel is OUT — the design correctly concedes this (OPT-D2 risk-flagged, full megakernel 'OUT'). What IS feasible in pure Triton on sm_121: (1) OPT-A JSON config tuning of the existing fp8 kernel — FEASIBLE NOW, lowest risk, no Hopper primitives; (2) OPT-C CUDA-graph full capture — FEASIBLE per the doc (rank 6 prototype), gated on OUR prealloc + GPU committer, must re-confirm on cu130-nightly (failed on 0.19); (3) OPT-B WY one-pass — FEASIBLE pure Triton static N_PAD<=16 (FR12 proved capture), hard effort. NOT feasible / risk-flagged: OPT-D2 cross-layer cp.async — vLLM #37431 reports OUR exact Mamba/Triton kernel family (_causal_conv1d_fwd/_chunk_scan_fwd/_chunk_state_fwd) throws cudaErrorIllegalInstruction in ASYNC mode on SM121, worked around only by enforce-eager (-37%); so aggressive Triton cp.async multi-stage is a live stability hazard on this exact codebase, not just a perf gamble. CRITICAL CONCEPTUAL ERROR in the design: if the forward is truly weight-bandwidth-bound (its own premise), cross-layer PREFETCH cannot beat the bandwidth floor — it can only HIDE launch/sync latency behind the weight stream, which is what CAPTURE (OPT-C) already does. Prefetch 'reclaiming bucket A ~55-75 ms' double-counts the launch/sync win that OPT-C claims; the same bytes still take 98.6 ms to read. The honest ceiling is set by how close capture+deep-staging gets the weight stream to peak, not by a separable 55-75 ms prefetch bucket.

The new OPT-D 'bucket A 55-75 ms reclaimable via cross-layer prefetch' is exactly the dropped lever — and is conceptually wrong: if weight-bandwidth-bound, prefetch only hides latency (capture's job), it cannot beat the 98.6 ms floor. The 55-75 ms 'prefetch bucket' overlaps OPT-C's launch/sync win. (2) BUCKET SPLIT UNMEASURED: nsys per-kernel export EMPTY; A/C/D sizing is literature-anchored estimate, and the runtime-API totals cited as evidence (cudaMalloc 55.9 s, cudaEventSync 26.1 s) are CUMULATIVE-over-capture incl. startup, NOT per-forward — a category slip when mapped onto 119.6 ms/fwd. (3) BUCKET D OVERCOUNTED: native already preserves run-ahead (0.8% main-thread block, overlapped OUTPUT-thread wait), so the ~15-30 ms 'sync gap' is near-zero on native; its slack concentrates in A+C. (4) achievableFloor 140-165 ms is a projection with no GB10 measurement; honest as a target, not a result. (5) Split-K/RevSplit-K GEMV (named as the OPT-A stretch + GemLite) is NOT bit-exact (cross-CTA combine reorders the fp32 K-reduction) and must be hard-excluded from the lossless path; only single-K-CTA config tuning is lossless. (6) OPT-D2 cross-layer cp.async hits the live vLLM #37431 sm_121 async illegal-instruction bug on OUR exact Mamba/Triton kernel family — a stability hazard, not just a perf risk. NET: native's 2.2x gap and OPT-A's lossless config win are real and worth building; the megakernel/cross-layer-prefetch fundamental is largely not GB10-feasible and partly double-counts capture, so holds=false on the design AS-STATED (megakernel framing + unmeasured 55-75 ms prefetch bucket), while the recommended OPT-A->OPT-C->OPT-B spine is sound.
